name: BTS6163D
title: PROFET BTS 6163 D: smart high-side power switch, 20 mΩ, with load-current sense
summary: A single-channel smart high-side switch for 24 V and 42 V systems: an N-channel power MOSFET with charge pump, switched on by pulling current out of its input, with an IS pin that sources a current proportional to load current (ratio about 9000) and a fixed fault current under overload, short circuit or overtemperature. It limits current, latches off on a hard short, shuts down and restarts on overtemperature, clamps inductive turn-off at 67 V below Vbb, survives 70 V load dump, and turns itself on under reverse battery. It comes in the 5-pin PG-TO252-5-11 (D-Pak) and is AEC qualified.

circuits.title: High-side switch with current sense
circuits.description: BTS6163D between the supply and a grounded load. Closing the input switch pulls current out of IN to logic ground and the output turns on. IS pushes a current proportional to load current into RIS, so VIS across RIS reads the load current against logic ground. The load returns to its own load ground.
notes: U1.Vbb is pin 3 and the tab; U1.OUT is pins 1 and 5 joined.

circuits.title: Connection with input resistor and sense resistor
circuits.description: The supply rail feeds pin 3. IN reaches the ground rail through RIN and the input switch, IS through RIS. OUT is the switched output; VON is the drop from Vbb to OUT and VOUT the output against ground. Two or more devices may be wired in parallel for a larger load current.

circuits.title: Overvoltage protection of the logic part
circuits.description: Parts outside the device that matter when the supply climbs past the internal 73 V zeners on IN and IS. RIN, optional, sits in the IN line. RIS takes IS to signal ground. RV and the zener VZ,VIS, both optional, carry the sense voltage on to a clamped node; without them IS can rise more than 5 V above ground once the overvoltage passes 73 V typ.
notes: Inside the device: Rbb = 100 Ω typ in the logic supply, VZ,IN = VZ,IS = 73 V typ.

circuits.title: Reverse battery protection (Reversave)
circuits.description: With the battery connected the wrong way round, current from signal ground flows into IN and IS, through the logic and Rbb, and switches the power transistor on, so the load current runs in the channel rather than the body diode. RIN in the input line and RIS on the sense pin set that current; the diode D across the NPN input switch passes the input share. RIN is added when the reverse supply is above 16 V.
notes: Recommended RIN for a reversed supply above 16 V: 1/RIN + 1/RIS = 0.08 A / (|Vbb| - 12 V). The total current into IN and IS is about 80 mA for low dissipation.

circuits.title: Inverse load current operation
circuits.description: An outside source holds OUT above Vbb, which is itself above 0 V, so load current flows backwards from OUT to Vbb. The input switch pulls IN to ground; RIS sits on IS. No sense current flows in this mode.

circuits.title: Vbb disconnect with an energised inductive load, version a
circuits.description: If the supply is broken while an inductive load is carrying current, that current needs a path rated for it. In version a, a diode D1 and a zener DZ1, joined anode to anode, sit across the load from OUT to ground. A single diode, a zener or a varistor may serve instead. With RIN = 0, VZL + VD has to stay below 63 V; for a higher clamp the IN and IS currents are limited to 120 mA.

circuits.title: Short circuit test circuit
circuits.description: The supply feeds Vbb through a primary impedance of 10 mΩ and 5 µH. OUT drives a secondary inductance LSC and resistance RSC into the load ZL; switch SC shorts the far end of RSC to ground. The input switch takes IN to ground; IS is left open.

circuits.title: Inductive load switch-off energy
circuits.description: An inductive load, L in series with RL, hangs from OUT. When the input switch opens, the output clamps at VON(CL) below Vbb and the device absorbs EAS: the energy taken from the supply while the load demagnetises, plus the energy stored in L, less what RL burns.

operation.text: An N-channel vertical power MOSFET with its own charge pump, a current-driven input and a load-current sense output, made as a Smart SIPMOS chip-on-chip device. The protection blocks are on chip: voltage source and sensor, overvoltage protection, current limit, gate protection, a clamp for unclamped inductive loads, output voltage detection and a temperature sensor.
Switching grounded DC loads in 42 V and 24 V systems with current-sense feedback: resistive, inductive and capacitive loads, in place of relays, fuses and discrete circuits. AEC qualified.

The output turns on when current is drawn out of IN to ground, normally through a switch. That switch has to handle 1.6 mA typ, 2.4 mA max. Below 30 µA of input current the device is off. A resistor RIN in series with IN limits the input slew rate and is needed for reverse-battery operation above 16 V.

Pins 1 and 5 are both OUT and must be joined outside. Leaving one open raises on-state resistance, lowers peak current capability and makes the sense output less accurate. Pin 3 and the tab are both Vbb, connected inside.
The switch shuts down when VbIN falls to VbIN(u), 2.5 V typ. Coming back up, the charge pump restarts at Vbb(ucp), 4 V typ.

In normal operation IS sources IL / kILIS into RIS, with kILIS about 9000. The internal circuit can drive this only while VOUT - VIS stays above 5 V, which caps RIS. The sense current saturates at IIS,lim. With a large RIS, VIS can approach Vbb. IS can be left open when sense is not used. For n devices in parallel RIS is 1 kΩ / n. IS does not give a valid reading during the settling times tson(IS) after turn-on and tslc(IS) after a load change; with the input off IS carries only the leakage IIS(LL). Calibrating kILIS for each device narrows the spread shown in the ratio curve, which covers all devices.

In overload (VON above 1 V typ), overtemperature or short-circuit shutdown with the input on, IS delivers a fixed IIS,fault of 5.2 mA typ instead of the proportional current, after tdelay(fault). As long as VbIS stays below VZ,IS the sense current does not exceed IIS,fault or IIS,lim. With an open load and the input on, IS carries only the offset IIS(LH).

When VON rises past 1 V typ but stays under VON(SC), the output stays on with the load current limited. The sense current first follows IL / kILIS, flattens at IIS,lim, and drops to IIS,fault once VON passes 1 V typ.

The load current is limited according to VON (typical characteristic). If VON exceeds VON(SC), 3.5 V typ, for longer than td(SC1), 650 µs typ after the input turns on, the output latches off. If a short appears while the output is already on, shutdown follows after td(SC2), 2 µs typ. The latch is cleared only by taking the input current to zero. Full short-circuit protection holds for supplies up to 48 V; the allowable secondary resistance and inductance depend on supply voltage.

Above the trip temperature Tjt, 175 °C typ, the output turns off and IS gives IIS,fault. It restarts by itself once the junction has cooled by the hysteresis, 10 K typ, and cycles this way while the input stays on.

At turn-off of an inductive load the output is clamped at VON(CL), 67 V typ, below Vbb, which demagnetises the load quickly. The energy absorbed is EAS; the maximum load inductance for one switch-off at a given current is given by its curve. The same clamp limits VON under supply overvoltage.

The logic is protected by zeners of 73 V typ from Vbb to IN (VZ,IN) and to IS (VZ,IS), fed through Rbb, 100 Ω typ, and rated for 15 mA. Beyond 73 V a voltage above 5 V can appear between IS and ground unless RV and a zener VZ,VIS are added. Load dump is rated at 70 V.

Under reversed supply the power MOSFET turns itself on, so the load current flows through the channel at RON(rev) rather than the body diode. The current that turns it on flows into IN and IS and through Rbb. To keep dissipation low, about 80 mA total into IN and IS is the target, provided by a small-signal diode across the input switch, a MOSFET input switch, or a suitable RIS. The heat from current in Rbb adds to the device's thermal load. Reverse supply is rated to 16 V without RIN.

With VOUT > Vbb > 0 V the device can run with load current flowing backwards. There is no sense current in this mode and no overtemperature protection. The body diode may conduct, so dissipation rises steeply. Back in forward mode the turn-on may be delayed by td(inv), 1 ms typ.

operation.topic: Loss of supply with an inductive load
operation.text: If Vbb is disconnected while an inductive load is energised, the load current needs its own path rated for it: a diode, a zener diode or a varistor. With RIN = 0, VZL + VD must stay below 63 V; for higher clamp voltages the currents into IN and IS are limited to 120 mA.

Also protected against loss of ground and loss of Vbb (the latter with an external diode for charged inductive loads), with ESD protection, very low standby current and optimised static EMC. The protections cover fault conditions outside normal operation and are not intended for continuous repeated use.
Two or more devices can be paralleled for more load current.

Turn-on time ton runs to 90 % of VOUT and turn-off time toff to 10 %; slew rates are measured between 25 % and 50 % of VOUT. At turn-off of an inductive load VOUT falls below ground and is held where VON equals VON(CL).
